verdict.rationale: Mastra is a workflow framework, so idempotency and exactly-once step semantics are a fair axis. The evidence only documents typed steps, retries, branches and suspend/resume. Nothing mentions idempotency keys, deduplication of duplicate triggers, or exactly-once step execution, and retries alone are an adjacent feature that does not prevent double-execution.

support.subject: As a backend developer, idempotency keys and exactly-once step semantics stop duplicate triggers from double-charging or double-sending
